title: Implement Post Read Time Estimation Feature
description: As part of an effort to improve user engagement on the ChronicleBoost blog platform, a new feature has been requested: displaying an estimated read time for each blog post. This common feature helps users decide whether to read an article based on their available time. The implementation will be split into two development sessions: first, handling the backend logic for calculation and storage, and second, updating the frontend to display this new information.

project_spec.name: ChronicleBoost
project_spec.description:
ChronicleBoost is an expert-level, high-performance web blog platform written entirely in C that transforms traditional blogging into a streamlined productivity hub. Beyond standard content publishing, it integrates task boards, calendar overlays, and contextual knowledge snippets so bloggers, editors, and readers can capture ideas, schedule drafts, and track editorial workflows without leaving the interface. The platform is designed around a strict hexagonal architecture: every external concern—database, HTTP, SMTP, payment provider, OAuth, or cache—plugs into the core through ports and adapters so feature work can progress rapidly while infrastructure can evolve independently.

Productivity is amplified through deep workflow automations: scheduled email digests, quick-capture file uploads, full-text search shortcuts, live markdown previews, and analytics-driven writing cues. Editors gain an admin panel that surfaces content health, caching heat-maps, and monetization metrics (via integrated payment processing). With powerful session management, SSL enforcement, and social logins, users can hop in instantly, draft, and publish securely from any device thanks to a responsive, SPA-style front-end compiled from WebAssembly modules generated by C code.
